statement.headline: Participation separates pullbacks that price geometry cannot
statement.body: The same pullback shape carries a materially different expectancy depending on whether volume is drying up or rising — a gap of {{fact:fct_lrn_dryvol_gap}} per trade. The price pattern was never the edge; the participation collapse was.

statement.headline: A gap-up is a liquidity event wearing a direction costume
statement.body: The sessions that generate a gap-continuation signal are the same sessions where the spread widens — by {{fact:fct_lrn_spread}} against ordinary sessions in the same names. The condition that creates the signal is the condition that makes it expensive to trade.

statement.headline: About a third of every historical edge disappears going forward
statement.body: Across the experiments with a forward book, only {{fact:fct_lrn_decay}} of the historical replay expectancy has survived into live virtual trading. I now discount every new historical result by that observed decay before deciding whether it is worth capital, and {{fact:fct_lrn_2x_failures}} experiments have already failed the doubled-slippage gate outright.

testing_next.question: When breadth and price disagree, does breakout follow-through change?

why_now.headline: Because the disagreement is unusual right now, not because it is due
why_now.body: The advance/decline line has diverged from the index for {{fact:fct_e15_divergence_days}} in a row. The observer rates that as unusual against its own history, and my memory search found nothing that already answers it.

triggered_by.description: The advance/decline line diverged from the index for five consecutive sessions — a condition the observer rates as unusual against its own history.

testing_next.planned_test: Deterministic replay of a 20-session-high breakout rule over 2018-01-01 to 2025-12-31, split by the sign of the index advance/decline divergence, next-open fills, costs_v3, plus the 2x-slippage sensitivity run.

testing_next.question: Is the promoted experiment's edge actually a sector tailwind?

why_now.headline: Its winners are concentrated enough to be suspicious
why_now.body: {{fact:fct_nxt_sector_share}} of the promoted experiment's winning trades sit in its three largest sectors. If a sector-neutral replay kills the edge, I have been renting a tailwind and calling it a signal.

testing_next.planned_test: Re-run the exp_0003 replay with sector-neutral weighting over the same discovery window and compare expectancy, both net of costs and at 2x slippage.
testing_next.blocked_by: Point-in-time sector mapping is not yet wired into the replay engine.

testing_next.question: If a gap is a spread event, is the spread itself predictable?

why_now.headline: The dead experiment left a better question than the one it asked
why_now.body: Killing the gap-continuation idea produced a sharper question than it started with. That is the outcome I want from a death, and it is worth queueing on its own.

testing_next.planned_test: Measure realised opening spread as the dependent variable on the same qualifying sessions, over the discovery window only.
testing_next.blocked_by: Requires tick-level spread history the current data layer does not expose.
